newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut arrests Palestinians for firing Katyusha.
newsitem.headline: Beirut arrests Palestinians for firing Katyusha.

text.p: Lebanese security forces arrested two members of a radical Palestinian group suspected of firing a Katyusha rocket into Israel this week, Lebanon's official National News Agency reported on Friday.

The agency, quoting judicial sources, said two members of the Damascus-based Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine (DFLP) were arrested and that they were being interrogated over Wednesday's Katyusha incident.
Judicial sources contacted by Reuters confirmed the report, adding that the two Palestinians were arrested in south Lebanon on Thursday. The DFLP is opposed to the Arab-Israeli peace talks.
Israel has blamed Lebanon for the rocket attack and an aide to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Thursday the Israeli army would do whatever was necessary to restore calm.
Lebanese leaders, anxious to avoid an escalation of violence between Moslem guerrillas and Israel in south Lebanon, have called for investigations into the cross-border attack.

Lebanon's pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) and the pro-Syrian Amal Movement -- both of which are fighting the Israeli occupation of a border zone in south Lebanon -- have denied any links to the Katyusha attack.
